note: Pool the builder draws one art direction from per video, skipping the ones in pipeline/history.json's last 5 entries. Each brief is a starting point: the palette still comes from the subject's own logos and artwork.

directions.name: Photocopied zine
directions.brief: Black-and-white photocopy texture, halftone dots, cut-out logos with rough paper edges, one spot colour from the subject's logo. Headlines set huge and tight, slightly rotated. Shots slam in like pages being slapped onto a desk.

directions.name: Pixel RPG quest
directions.brief: The video is a quest: each step is a level, options are characters with stat bars, the verdict is a boss fight or a treasure chest. Chunky pixel frames, stepped (not eased) motion, a pixel display face only for headlines.

directions.name: Engineer's notebook
directions.brief: Squared paper, hand-drawn boxes and arrows drawn on with stroke animation, sticky notes for asides, highlighter swipes on key words. Logos taped in. Feels like someone explaining on paper.

directions.name: Ops console
directions.brief: Dense monitoring dashboard: panels, live-looking counters, log lines scrolling, status lights. Comparisons as two services' health panels. Mono for data, a wide grotesk for headlines. Real commands typed in the terminal.

directions.name: Retro desktop OS
directions.brief: Windows 98 / classic Mac desktop: every fact is a window or dialog box that pops open, buttons, title bars, a progress bar for install steps, a fake error dialog as the hook.

directions.name: Sports broadcast
directions.brief: Head-to-head match: lower-thirds, scoreboard that updates per round, 'round 1/2/3' cards, a final score. Bold condensed type, team colours taken from each subject's logo.

directions.name: Transit map
directions.brief: The topic is a metro map: each option is a line in its logo colour, features are stations, the install is a route with stops. Thick rounded lines drawn on, clean sans, lots of white space.

directions.name: Shop receipt
directions.brief: Thermal receipt printing out line by line: features as items, costs and limits as prices, the verdict as the total. Mono type, torn edge, a barcode at the end. Paper on a dark counter.

directions.name: Magazine spread
directions.brief: Each shot is a magazine cover or spread: giant masthead-style headline, cover lines around a hero image of the logo, page numbers. Strong serif display with a plain sans for cover lines.

directions.name: VHS tape
directions.brief: Recorded-off-TV look: tracking lines and chroma bleed on edges, a PLAY or FF flash only on a cut. Chapters as tape counter jumps that sit in the shot, not a REC label or timestamp left on screen. Keep the text itself sharp and readable above the noise.

directions.name: Trading cards
directions.brief: Each option is a collectible card with art, type, and stats that flips to show its back; comparisons as two cards side by side with stats lighting up. Card frames tinted from each logo.

directions.name: Blueprint
directions.brief: Technical drawing: blue paper, white line work, dimension lines and callouts pointing at parts of a diagram of how the thing works. Lines draw on; labels in a narrow technical sans.

directions.name: Group chat
directions.brief: The whole video plays as a messaging thread: the question arrives as a message, answers as bubbles, logos as avatars, commands as code blocks someone pastes. Typing indicators between beats.

directions.name: Kinetic type
directions.brief: Almost no imagery: words are the visuals. Huge type that fills the frame, words swapping on the voice's beat, one word per beat at key moments, colour flips between shots. Logos appear only as punctuation.

directions.name: 3D product shots
directions.brief: Real 3D with the kit's Stage3D: each tool is an object on a turntable or a plinth (its avatar as a texture on a slab, a coin or a box), lit like a product photo against a deep backdrop in the logo's colour. The camera dollies and orbits slowly; cuts change the angle. Text stays flat HTML laid over the scene, set large and sparse.

directions.name: Server room flythrough
directions.brief: Real 3D with the kit's Stage3D: racks, blinking status lights and cables built from simple boxes and planes, low-key light with one coloured key light from the subject's logo. The camera glides down an aisle and stops on the rack that matters for each line. Commands appear on a flat terminal laid over the scene.

directions.name: Floating 3D diagram
directions.brief: Real 3D with the kit's Stage3D: the topic as a diagram floating in space, with tools as thick tiles carrying their avatars, connected by tubes or arcs, seen from a tilted isometric camera that swings to each part as the voice reaches it. Clean, bright, matte materials; flat HTML labels beside the tiles.

pacing: Fast cuts: a new shot or visual change at least every 1.5s.
Few long shots: 3–5 shots, each building up in place.
Chapters: a title card before each section, then quick shots inside it.
